text:
maria: quick follow-up to the principal routing RFC — thinking about mapping API keys to 'intents' rather than strictly to project/org roles. want feedback on tradeoffs.
kevin: intent-based keys = interesting. can you sketch a concrete example?
maria: sure. imagine keys carry a small intent set: ["ingest-embeddings", "read-models"]. not full roles, just allowed intents. runtime enforces intent->route mapping.
sam: how do you see this overlaying RBAC? is intent an orthogonal check or replacement?
maria: orthogonal. RBAC still controls fine-grained resource access; intents are a routing/usage gate to reduce blast radius and simplify rate/cost controls.
tara: worry: runtime cost of additional intent checks on hot paths. we already do API key -> project lookup + quota. adding intent evaluation could add latency.
maria: good point. design idea: encode a compact intent bitmap in the key metadata so checks are bitwise masked at the gateway. no extra DB hop for common paths.
kevin: so the key contains an intent-bitset id, then gateway has a small in-memory map of bitset defs per tenant? that seems fast. what about rotation and revocation?
maria: rotation is unchanged (rotate secret + rebind metadata). revocation requires invalidating in-memory map; we can use a pub/sub invalidate channel (existing auth-cache invalidation).
sam: operationally, how do we avoid permission creep? product teams might stack many intents on a single key. we need defaults and caps.
maria: propose limits: intent cardinality limit per key (e.g., max 4), and an intent approval flow for >2 intents. mirrors current quota approval.
tara: migration plan? we have thousands of long-lived keys with project-level permissions.
maria: dual-mode rollout: 1) accept legacy keys (project-scoped) and map them internally to a broadened intent bucket; 2) encourage new keys to be intent-first. provide an automated shim that translates legacy project policy to inferred intents for a period of 6 months.
kevin: any privacy/telemetry impact? intent metadata will increase audit surface. that's probably good for SRE but might leak too much in some orgs.
maria: intent is only a short label set; we can opt-in telemetry at org level. default: collect intent usage counts but redact exact keys.
sam: edge case: cross-project service calls where a service legitimately needs to act across projects (platform services). intents alone won't capture actor identity.
maria: correct — for cross-project calls we require both intent AND an actor-level delegation token (ephemeral) which includes project scope. intent gates the route, delegation asserts the project-level authority.
tara: sounds complex but manageable. quick question: how does this interact with function/tool-calling-style requests where a single call may trigger multiple downstream intents?
maria: gateway computes the union of required intents from the request envelope before routing; we treat the request as needing the superset. if missing intents, gateway rejects 403 with structured error: {"missing_intents": [...]}.
kevin: example config snippet for key metadata?
maria: sure: 
```
key_metadata:
  id: key_abc123
  intents: [ingest-embeddings, rerank]
  max_qps: 20
  org_id: org_42
```
kevin: looks good. one more nit: billing. per-intent billing or still per-token? customers will ask.
maria: keep per-token billing. intents only influence routing, rate limits, and cost-controls (e.g., prioritize low-cost models for ingest-intent). no change to metering schema initially.
sam: ops questions: how do we test in staging? need a simulator for intent bitsets + legacy shim.
maria: plan: small staging rollout with feature-flagged gateway. add fuzz tests that randomize intent sets and ensure no unintended resource access. also run integration with telemetry to validate counts.
tara: +1 on fuzz tests. also add an RBAC safety net: even if intent allows route, the resource-level RBAC must still be checked downstream (defense in depth).
maria: agreed — intent is an allow-list for routing only. downstream RBAC is authoritative.
kevin: thumbs up. can we capture this as a follow-up doc (short RFC addendum) and allocate a spike to prototype the in-memory map + invalidation?
maria: i'll draft the addendum with the config snippet and migration steps. want a 2-week spike (kevin + tara volunteering?).
kevin: me.
tara: me.
auth-bot: deploy-check: feature-flag `intent-routing` created in staging. use `ff-rollout` to enable for org_42 when ready. :package:
